_meta.indication: MOUNJARO is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trial; subjects randomized 1:1:1:1 to tirzepatide 5, 10, or 15 mg or placebo SC QW over a 40-week treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, naive to antihyperglycemic injectable therapy, inadequately controlled with diet and exercise alone and not treated with any oral antihyperglycemic medication during the three months preceding trial start.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change in HbA1c from baseline at 40 weeks (superiority of tirzepatide vs placebo).
pivotal_trials.n: mITT per arm: placebo 113; tirzepatide 5 mg 121; 10 mg 121; 15 mg 120
pivotal_trials.result: HbA1c change at Week 40: placebo -0.09%, tirzepatide 5 mg -1.75%, 10 mg -1.71%, 15 mg -1.69%. FDA-analyzed difference from placebo: 5 mg -1.64 (95% CI -1.94, -1.34); 10 mg -1.60 (95% CI -1.90, -1.30); 15 mg -1.59 (95% CI -1.90, -1.28); all p<0.001. HbA1c <7% achieved by 81.8%, 84.5%, 78.3% of the 5/10/15 mg arms vs 23.0% placebo (p<0.001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%): nausea, diarrhea, decreased appetite, vomiting, constipation, dyspepsia, and abdominal pain. In placebo-controlled trials nausea occurred in 12%/15%/18% (5/10/15 mg) vs 4% placebo, and diarrhea in 12%/13%/17% vs 9% placebo. GI adverse reactions led to discontinuation in 3.0% (5 mg), 5.4% (10 mg), and 6.6% (15 mg) of patients.
target_moa: Tirzepatide is a glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist; it selectively binds to and activates both the GIP and GLP-1 receptors, the targets for native GIP and GLP-1. It is the first-in-class agent to activate both incretin receptor types.
modality: Peptide (39-amino acid modified peptide with a C20 fatty diacid moiety enabling albumin binding).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF THYROID C-CELL TUMORS. Tirzepatide causes thyroid C-cell tumors in rats; it is unknown whether MOUNJARO causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans. MOUNJARO is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of MTC or in patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).

rems.type: No REMS is recommended for this product; a Risk Management Plan was not provided and FDA concluded no additional REMS was necessary, with safety concerns addressed through labeling and routine pharmacovigilance.

advisory_committee.vote: This Application was not discussed at an advisory committee meeting.

description.text: Expanded the type 2 diabetes indication to include pediatric patients aged 10 years and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the Prescribing Information (PI) and Medication Guide (MG) based on the results of trial 18F-MC-GPGV, titled, A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 3 Study With an Open-Label Extension Assessing the Efficacy, Safety, and Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamics of Tirzepatide in Pediatric and Adolescent Participants With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Inadequately Controlled With Metformin, or Basal Insulin, or Both, including expansion of the currently approved indication to include pediatric patients aged 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus. basis.text: The NDA was designated Priority (Priority review), with a PDUFA goal date of May 15, 2022.

summary.text: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA received September 15, 2021 and reviewed under Priority review with a PDUFA goal date of May 15, 2022, and was approved during the first review cycle for glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes. It was not an accelerated approval and was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: Your application for Mounjaro was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.
